summary: Right-clicking the Back or Forward toolbar button opens a menu of the places it leads to, nearest first, at most twelve, and choosing one goes there in one step. Each button's tooltip names the place a click leads to, ahead of the keys. src/model.rs: History::back_by / forward_by (all or nothing; back() and forward() are *_by(1)) and back_list / forward_list (nearest first). src/finder/mod.rs: go_back_by / go_forward_by (pub(super)) hold what go_back / go_forward did, and the two actions call them with 1. src/finder/toolbar.rs: each nav button sits in a wrapper (div#back-history, div#forward-history) that carries the kit context menu; history_places, history_labels, distinct_end, history_tip, history_menu and with_history_menu are free functions above `impl Finder`. docs/manual.md: the Toolbar table's Back, Forward row and a bullet under Toolbar menus. examples/screenshot.rs and examples/drive.rs take a `right-click:<id>` step.
changelog: Right-click the Back or Forward button for a menu of the places it leads to, nearest first, and choose one to go straight there instead of a step at a time. The menu lists up to twelve places, and a folder with the same name as another place in it shows the folder it is in, as in "src — atlas". Each button's tooltip names the place a click leads to, such as Back to "Projects".
behaviour_changes: Menu. Right-click Back or Forward with somewhere to go: a menu opens at the pointer with up to 12 places, nearest first. A click on one, or Down/Up and Return, goes there in one step. The history ends as after that many single steps, only the place arrived at is listed, and a search in progress ends as with Back.
Selection. After Back by menu the folder gone into from the destination is selected (for one step that is the folder just left, as before). After Forward nothing is selected, as before.

Labels. A place is listed by its name (folder name, Recents, Trash, a results title). A folder that shares its name with a different place in the menu reads `src — atlas`, or `src — atlas/lib` when the folders they are in share a name too; a folder named like the Trash reads `Trash — <its folder>` beside `Trash`. The same folder listed twice keeps its plain name.
Menu width. At least 200 pt; it grows up to the window's width, less the kit's 8 px margins, for a long name.
Tooltips. `Back to “atlas”` / `Forward to “Projects”`, followed by the keys as before (Alt+Left / Alt+Right on Linux). With nowhere to go they stay `Back` / `Forward`.
Right-click with nowhere to go. Nothing opens and the keyboard stays where it was. Before, that press took the keyboard from the files.

Right-click on an enabled button no longer gives the button the keyboard. Escape, a click outside, or a choice returns the keyboard to whatever had it: the files, the search field, a Tab-focused button, or the other pane in split view.
Menu left open while the history changes under it (Alt+Left, the mouse's side buttons): an item whose place is no longer that many steps away does nothing, and the menu closes.

Review fix: the menu closes when its window changes size, with the keyboard back where it was. Without that the menu vanished and kept the keyboard, and no key worked until the next click, because the kit draws a context menu only while its trigger is under the pressed point and these buttons are right-aligned. A window that only moves, or becomes active or inactive, keeps its menu.
Linux windows whose title bar fffinder draws: a right-click on Back or Forward no longer shows the window menu; empty toolbar space still does. From reading, not run.
Unchanged: left click, the keys and the mouse's side buttons, and the nav pill's width (the measuring toolbar test passes).
Examples: `--do right-click:<id>` in examples/screenshot.rs (so in shot.sh) and `right-click:<id>` in examples/drive.rs.
left_out: CHANGELOG.md is not edited, per the guide. The entry is in this record and in the commit message.
Other ways to open the menu: click-and-hold (Finder's gesture) and a key are not in the brief. Once open, the menu works from the keyboard.
Nothing was compiled or run for macOS or Windows. The change has no cfg-specific code and removes or renames nothing; the unit test's expectations use MAIN_SEPARATOR.

Layout changes made by a key under an open menu. Keys still reach the window while any menu is open. In a window about 900 pt wide, Cmd+Alt+S under an open history menu re-fits the toolbar, the button moves from under the pressed point, and the menu is gone with the keyboard in it until a click (probed). This is the kit's behaviour for every context menu in the app (the item menu does it after Cmd+2), so it is left to focus-lost-recovery; see notes.
A right-click in the nav pill's 2 pt padding or in the gap between the two buttons opens nothing and gives the keyboard to the browser as a whole, as a right press on any chrome did before (probed).

Touch long press, from reading only: the kit's context menu also opens on a long press, and only the right mouse press is guarded. On a button with nowhere to go that would still open the undrawn empty menu.

Very long folder names: the menu grows to the window's width and the name is cut at the window's edge with no ellipsis; the tooltip can outgrow the window and push the key hint out, as the existing `Search Only in “name”` tooltip does.
A stale item does nothing even when its place could still be reached by another count.

On Windows a folder directly in a drive's root that shares its name with a place that is not a folder (a folder named Trash beside the Trash) would read `Trash — \`, without the drive letter. From reading; two folders in two drives' roots read `src — C:\` and `src — D:\`.
tests: src/model.rs: model::tests::history_goes_several_places_at_once (lists nearest first; back_by and forward_by all or nothing, zero steps included; two at once end where two single steps do). Mutations caught: back_by without .rev(), forward_by going as far as it can.
src/finder/toolbar.rs: finder::toolbar::tests::a_history_menu_tells_folders_with_one_name_apart (mutation caught: the folder always appended)

tests/controls.rs: back_and_forward_buttons_list_their_history. Without the change it fails at 'after a right-click on back': the old code gave up the files' keyboard on a right press on the disabled button.
tests/controls.rs: a_history_menu_lists_the_twelve_nearest_places. Without the change: no labels.
tests/controls.rs: a_history_menu_goes_only_where_it_says. Without the change: no labels. Without the click-time check it lands on the fixture folder instead of Projects.

tests/controls.rs: a_history_menu_closes_when_the_window_changes_size (added in review). Without the window observer it fails at 'the keyboard is back with the files'; with the observer but without its size comparison it fails at the last line, where an activation closes the menu.
review_fixes: src/finder/toolbar.rs history_menu: the menu now closes when its window changes size. Found by a probe: with a history menu open, a window made 120 pt narrower left no menu on screen and the keyboard in it, so Escape, Down and Alt+Left did nothing until a click. The kit draws a context menu only while its trigger's bounds hold the pressed point (ContextMenu::prepaint, draws_menu), and Back and Forward keep to the window's right edge, so any change of width takes them from under it. The builder registers cx.observe_window_bounds on the menu and, when the size differs from the one the menu was built at and the menu has the keyboard, sends the kit's Cancel action, which is what Escape sends: the kit dismisses the menu and gives the keyboard back. The size comparison matters: a window reports its bounds on a move and on every change of active status too (gpui-pre window.rs, on_active_status_change calls bounds_changed), and without it my first version closed the menu whenever the window went inactive or active, which on a platform that delivers the click before the activation would close a menu the moment it opened.

tests/controls.rs: added a_history_menu_closes_when_the_window_changes_size, beside the other history tests. It pins both halves: the resize closes the menu and the files' keys work, and an activation leaves the menu open.
src/finder/toolbar.rs history_menu: the menu's widest is the window's width less px(16.), not ui(16.). The 16 is the kit's two 8 px margins around a menu, which don't grow with Settings › Text size.
Commit message: the paragraph on what had to be kept from happening now has the fourth case, the window changing size, and its last sentence the fourth remedy.
No change to the implementer's model, navigation, labels, guards, manual text or examples. I found nothing wrong in them.
notes:
Checked. check.sh printed CHECK OK on the trunk commit 69b956f: 533 passed in 16 test binaries, 3 of 3 known root-only failures. The trunk had moved by one commit while I reviewed (9cf7635, escape-ends-search); the rebase had no conflicts, I ran check.sh again on the result and probed the two changes together (below). Pushed to origin (9cf7635..69b956f). The implementer's commit was d7ade2b; the trunk commit differs from it by the review fixes above.

How it was checked. With the src diff reverse-applied on the final commit all four UI tests fail (controls.rs:73 'after a right-click on back', :126 and :145 no labels, :169 no menu) and with it back the tree is clean; the three unit tests cannot exist without the change. Thirteen mutations of the final code, one at a time, each failed a kept test: no prevent_default on the right press; no empty-menu guard; no click-time check; ix + 2 steps; the two lists swapped; nothing selected after Back; no window observer; no size comparison in it; thirteen places; back_by without .rev(); forward_by going as far as it can; the folder always appended; the Forward menu stepping back. The four UI tests pass under SEED 0, 1, 7, 42, 99 and 1234, and the new one in 20 iterations. Probes, in a throwaway test file that is deleted: Forward's menu opened while Back's is open and the other way round (the first closes, the keyboard ends with the files); a right-click on a button with no history while the Sort menu is open (Sort closes, the files keep the keyboard); during a search with the field focused (Escape closes only the menu and typing goes on in the field; a choice ends the search, goes there, and the field keeps the keyboard, exactly as a click on Back does); Down, Down, Return and Up, Return; split view (each pane lists its own history, and the keyboard stays in the pane that had it); a name being edited (the press ends the edit as any click does, the menu opens, Escape leaves the keyboard with the files); Recents, the Trash and a results place by name, there and back; a Tab-focused Back button (it keeps the keyboard through its menu, keeps it when the choice disables it, and Tab moves on); the mouse's Back button pressed outside an open menu (the menu closes and the window goes back one); the window going inactive and active with a menu open (it stays); a resize of an inactive and of an active window, of height only, and a resize after the menu was closed while the search field had words in it (the words stay: no Cancel reaches the field); the same over an empty focused search field on top of 9cf7635 (Escape closes the menu, the next Escape leaves for the files; a resize closes the menu and typing goes to the field). I took five pictures of my own from the final build (Back menu light, Forward menu dark, tooltip, no history, same names dark, in a scratch copy of the demo) and compared them with the implementer's eighteen, which are the ones kept.

The three ways I thought this most likely to hurt someone, and what the code says. (1) The keyboard left in something that isn't drawn, or handed to the wrong thing. The right-press listener on each button runs before the button's own focus listener and before the kit menu's (both are registered earlier in paint, and bubbling runs last-registered first), so prevent_default keeps the press from focusing an enabled button and stop_propagation keeps an empty menu from opening at all; a disabled kit Button tracks no focus, so before this change that press fell through to the browser's root. The menu restores what had the keyboard when it opened, and PopupMenu::dismiss leaves it alone if the item's handler moved it. The case the code did not cover was the menu's button moving from under it, which the review fix closes for a window that changes size. What remains is in left_out and under focus-lost-recovery below. (2) Landing somewhere other than the place named. Item ix takes ix + 1 steps of an all-or-nothing back_by/forward_by, whose drain(..).rev() I checked by hand and the unit test checks against single steps; the lists are read nearest first for both the menu and the tooltip; and each item acts only while history_places(..).get(ix) is still the Location it was built for, so a history that moved on under the menu (keys and the mouse's side buttons still reach the window) makes the item do nothing. A history that follows a renamed folder changes the Location too, so those items also do nothing. (3) Plain Back and Forward made worse. go_back and go_forward keep their signatures and call the *_by twins with 1; the selection after one step is the same folder as before, because end_search does not touch the history and the first forward entry after a step back is the place just left. A right press never fires on_click (gpui takes only the left button for clicks). The tooltip still goes through tooltip_with_action, so the keys show (pictures). The wrappers are flex_none around fixed-size buttons and the_toolbar_folds_just_when_the_drawn_controls_run_out_of_room still measures the same pill. Nothing per frame but two short strings for the tooltips; display_name does no I/O.

Doubts that remain, for the owner. (a) Nothing ran on macOS or Windows. On a Mac check once: a two-finger click on Back opens the menu, the tooltip reads Back to “name” with Cmd+[, and resizing the window with the menu open closes it. (b) The menu closes on any change of the window's size, of height alone too, though only a change of width moves the buttons. I kept the rule simple. (c) The labels depart from the plan of record, which appended the whole tildified path; the implementer's shortest telling-apart end (`src — atlas`) reads better in the common case and I kept it. If whole paths are wanted, history_labels is the one place. (d) On a Linux window whose title bar fffinder draws, a right-click on Back or Forward no longer shows the window menu, with or without history. (e) A right-click that misses the buttons by a point or two, in the pill's padding or gap, opens nothing and takes the keyboard from the files as before. The pill could take the same right-press guard if near misses turn out to matter.

For briefs still to come.
- back-forward-restore-search: read `git show 69b956f` before you plan. History now has back_by(steps) and forward_by(steps), all or nothing, with back() and forward() as *_by(1), and back_list() / forward_list() yielding &Location nearest first. Finder::go_back_by / go_forward_by hold the bodies of go_back / go_forward; the selection after Back is read from history.forward_list().next() after the move, not from current_folder() before it. In toolbar.rs, history_places(finder, forward) clones the twelve nearest Locations and is read in three places that must keep agreeing: the menu builder, the empty-menu guard on each button's right press, and every item's click-time check, which compares Locations. history_labels and history_tip name a place by Location::title(). With visits that carry a search you need: wording for a visit that is a search, in the menu and in the tooltip (history_tip gets back_list().next()); a decision on the step that pops nothing (Back during a search only ends it), because the menu's item ix means ix + 1 single steps and the first thing Back does must be the first thing the menu lists and the tooltip names; the guard to agree with the button's enabled state, since `can_back() || is_searching()` enables Back with an empty back stack and a right-click on it must then either list that step or stay guarded, or the undrawn empty menu takes the keyboard for good; and the click-time check to compare whatever makes a visit (place and search), not the place alone. Tests that pin the present behaviour: model::tests::history_goes_several_places_at_once (back_by(2) equals two back()s), and in tests/controls.rs back_and_forward_buttons_list_their_history (labels, the selection, can_go_back() false at the start folder), a_history_menu_lists_the_twelve_nearest_places and a_history_menu_goes_only_where_it_says. Probed today: from a search, a choice in the menu ends the search and goes to the place, and the search field keeps the keyboard if it had it.
- focus-lost-recovery: your plan says menus are unaffected because PopupMenu restores focus when dismissed. That holds for a dismissed menu, not for one that stops being drawn while it has the keyboard, and the kit stops drawing a context menu as soon as its trigger's bounds no longer hold the point that was pressed (gpui-component menu/context_menu.rs, draws_menu) or the trigger itself is gone. Probed: right-click a file for its menu, press Cmd+2 (as List), and Down, Cmd+1 and every other key do nothing until a click (that is the item menu, which this change does not touch); and with a history menu open in a window about 900 pt wide, Cmd+Alt+S re-fits the toolbar and a second Cmd+Alt+S can't bring the sidebar back. This change closes the history menus when the window changes size, so that one case never reaches you; the others do. From reading, not run: in these cases focus_lost_restore_target is not `this.focus`. The kit registers a never-focused handle on the ContextMenu element's own dispatch node every frame (prepaint, set_focus_handle with trigger_focus_handle) and the menu's node is below it, so while the trigger is still drawn that handle is the restore target; when the trigger is gone it is the nearest drawn ancestor with a handle, files_focus for a file's menu. With the plan's strict `h == this.focus` neither is rescued. A second arm for a target that is inside this browser and is neither the files, the tree nor a field would cover the first; think about whether a lost menu over the files should count as well. The kit's menu state stays open either way: probed, a history menu left open through Cmd+\ twice comes back into view, unfocused, when its button is under the pressed point again, and a click anywhere closes it. The implementer's remark that your recovery would also rescue the empty menu a touch long press can open is only true with the wider match.
- split-view-toolbar-clip: the nav pill's two buttons each sit in a `div().id("back-history" | "forward-history").flex_none()` inside a kit ContextMenu element; the pill's width is unchanged. The menu is drawn at the pressed point only while the button is still under it, so a toolbar that re-fits or a pane that changes width without the window changing size (your fifth fold, the sidebar's new cap) moves the buttons from under an open menu; see focus-lost-recovery above. The menu's widest is the window's width (viewport_size), not the pane's: it is a window-level popup that snaps to the window. In tests `ui.right_click("back")` is ambiguous in split view: use `window.within("split-pane").right_click("back", cx)` for the split pane and the leftmost of find_all for the first.
- split-active-pane: a right-click on a pane's Back or Forward leaves the keyboard in whichever pane had it, and so does a choice in the menu, as the toolbar's other menus do (probed: the split pane went back, the first pane's files kept the keys). If the active pane should follow, the item handler in history_menu is the place, and the click-time check must stay ahead of it. With your tab_stop on files_focus: Back and Forward are tab stops today; a Tab-focused Back keeps the keyboard through its menu and keeps it when a choice disables it, and Tab then moves on (probed).
- context-menus-fit: the kit's menus do not cut long item text. The history menu avoids the overflow with `.max_w(window width - px(16.))`; a name wider than the window is cut at the window's edge with no ellipsis. If you add a way to fit long labels in menus, history_labels (toolbar.rs) is where these are made, and its menu could then drop max_w. For your empty Recents menu in a chooser: here the trigger is always wrapped and a right-press listener on the child stops the press when the menu would be empty, which keeps the element path the same whether or not there is something to list.
- recent-searches: toolbar.rs gained about 150 lines above `impl Finder` and the two nav children of the pill are now `with_history_menu(..)` calls, so your line numbers are off; find things by name. `view_mode_items` is unchanged. A menu you open with the kit's context_menu has the same life as this one: drawn only while its trigger is under the pressed point. The search field is right-aligned like these buttons, so if your menu is a context menu on the magnifier, a window that changes width with it open leaves the keyboard in a menu that isn't drawn; a popover or dropdown anchored to its trigger does not have this. If you do use a context menu, the observer at the top of history_menu is the remedy and a_history_menu_closes_when_the_window_changes_size shows how to pin it.
- tab-drop-and-close, tab-bar-overflow: a tab's right-click menu is a kit context menu too. In my probe three tabs kept their width through a resize and the menu stayed; with tabs that shrink or scroll from under the pressed point the menu would go undrawn with the keyboard in it, as described above. If your change makes tabs move more, probe it.
- restore-session-tabs: History::last_folder() can sit beside back_list(); `self.back.iter().rev()` is nearest first. Workspace already observes the window's bounds (remember_placement); each open history menu adds one detached observer of its own, which goes once its menu entity has been dropped, at the next open of that menu.
- inactive-selection-colour, and anyone taking pictures: shot.sh takes `--do right-click:<element id>` now, and the menu is in the picture. IDs that are a name and a number can't be given.

Found, not fixed (all there before this change).
- Keys reach the window while any menu is open, and a kit context menu whose trigger moves or goes is no longer drawn but keeps the keyboard: the item menu after Cmd+2 leaves every key dead until a click (probed). The menu also stays open in the kit's state and reappears when its trigger is back under the pressed point.
- A right or middle press on chrome that is not a control gives the keyboard to the browser as a whole, where shortcuts work and arrows don't; the scope-chips-keep-focus record has this too. It now includes the nav pill's padding and gap.
- A right-click on any other toolbar button gives that button the keyboard (the implementer's finding; the same guard as here would stop it).
- Disabled pill buttons are drawn like enabled ones: Back and Forward with nowhere to go look the same as with somewhere to go (seen in my no-history picture). pill_button sets the text colour, which overrides the kit's disabled colour.
- The implementer reports that `Cut “name”` and similar item-menu labels run out of the menu for long names; I did not look at it.
- GUIDE.md's list of shot.sh steps mentions neither `hover:` nor `right-click:`.

Housekeeping. My temporary files were in lane-f-history-menus in the shared scratchpad, which I deleted; I touched nothing outside it. The probes were throwaway tests in tests/zz_probe_history.rs, removed before every check; the mutation runs restored the three source files from saved copies and I compared them byte for byte. The lane is clean and at the trunk's tip. The first `git push origin` was refused by the session's permission check when it was part of a longer command; sent alone it went through.
